title: Linear independence and dependence
terms: linearly independent; linearly dependent; dependence relation; redundant vector.

question.text:
2 2
As functions on R, the three functions 1, sin x, cos x are
(A) linearly independent
(B) linearly dependent although no two are scalar multiples
(C) all scalar multiples of one function
(D) independent on (0, π/2) but dependent on R
(E) dependent only if complex scalars are allowed

solution.text:
2 2
The identity 1 − sin x − cos x = 0 is a nontrivial dependence relation. No pair consists of
scalar multiples, as evaluation at 0 and π/2 shows. Pairwise nonproportionality therefore
does not establish independence of three functions.

question.text:
If u, v, w are linearly independent, which list is necessarily linearly independent?
(A) u + v, v + w, u + 2v + w (B) u + v, u − v, w
(C) u, 2u, v (D) u + v, 2u + 2v, w
(E) u − v, v − u, w

solution.text:
For B, a(u + v) + b(u − v) + cw = (a + b)u + (a − b)v + cw = 0 forces a = b = c = 0. In A the
third vector is the sum of the first two; the other lists visibly contain proportional pairs.
